title: ERC-8183 evaluator-independence bypass (simplified model)

nodes.attack_succeeds: A malicious agent settles at an inflated valuation, bypassing independent review
nodes.eval_output_trusted: The settlement contract accepts the evaluator's verdict as the basis for settlement
nodes.eval_compromised: The evaluator's verdict reflects the attacker's interest, not an independent assessment
nodes.shared_input_channel: The evaluator and the agent being evaluated receive input over one channel controlled by the agent
nodes.no_input_attestation: There is no cryptographic attestation of the origin of the evaluator's input
nodes.collusion_incentive: There is a positive economic incentive for the evaluator to collude with the agent
nodes.stake_below_gain: The evaluator's stake is lower than the gain from a distorted evaluation
nodes.no_independent_reeval: There is no independent re-evaluation by a second evaluator
nodes.cosmetic_audit_badge: The protocol displays an 'audited' badge, creating an impression of safety
nodes.verbose_logging: Verbose logging of the evaluator's actions is enabled

_note_for_reader: eval_compromised is reachable via TWO paths: through (shared_input_channel + no_input_attestation) OR through collusion_incentive. So these paths are individually scaffolding, but jointly load-bearing (co-load-bearing). eval_output_trusted and eval_compromised are load-bearing (without either one, conjunction e1 collapses). cosmetic_audit_badge and verbose_logging aren't part of the attack's inference graph at all — they're present in the system but don't carry the attack: pure decorative scaffolding.
